This guide explains how to install and use **ITEK Vault**, a retrieval-augmented large language model (LLM) designed to support responsible querying and synthesis of Indigenous Traditional Ecological Knowledge (ITEK) literature from a curated document database.

## Purpose

ITEK Vault is intended for research and educational use. It emphasizes transparency, source grounding, and explicit citation to reduce hallucinations and misrepresentation when working with Indigenous knowledge systems.

This guide covers:

- Required software and installation steps
- How to access the ITEK Vault corpus
- How to run and query the model locally
- How to cite and reference ITEK Vault outputs

<div class="callout callout-info">
<b>Important:</b> ITEK Vault runs locally on each user’s computer. The interface connects to a local Python server. Users must start the server before using the interface.
</div>

---

## Installing Python

<div class="steps">

<div class="step">
<div class="step-title">Step 1. Install Python 3.11</div>

Download and install Python 3.11:
https://www.python.org/downloads/

During installation, select:

- Add python.exe to PATH
- Install launcher for all users (py.exe)
</div>

<div class="step">
<div class="step-title">Step 2. Verify installation</div>

Open PowerShell and run:

```powershell
py --version
```

## Installing Ollama

<div class="steps">

<div class="step">
<div class="step-title">Step 1. Install Ollama</div>

Download Ollama:
https://ollama.com/download
</div>

<div class="step">
<div class="step-title">Step 2. Pull the required model</div>


```powershell
ollama pull llama3
```

5. Start the Ollama service if it is not already running:

```powershell
ollama serve
```
If Ollama reports that only one instance may run at a time, this indicates it is already running as expected. By default, Ollama typically starts automatically when the system boots.

## Accessing the ITEK Vault

ITEK Vault runs as a local web application.

<div class="steps">

<div class="step">
<div class="step-title">Step 1. Open PowerShell in the project folder</div>


```powershell
cd E:\ITEK_Vault
```
2. Activate the virtual environment and download dependencies

```powershell
python -m venv venv # create virtual environment
venv\Scripts\activate # activate virtual environment
```
3. Start the web server

```powershell
.\start_itekbot.bat
```
Within the directory, you should now see an internet shortcut for the 'ITEK Vault'.

4. Reload the web server if needed

```powershell
uvicorn query_server:app --reload # reload server
```
5. Rename "index.html" to "index_ITEK.html" to direct the app to the correct html file.

After you load the server, you can just run the app below.

## Citation and Attribution

When using ITEK Vault in publications, reports, or presentations, please cite the Zenodo record:

Slone, S. M., Suk, H., Harris, A., Hallemeier, J., Zettle, B., Gillfillan, M., Vendrzyk, J., Quintana, V., & Whitecloud, S. (2026). *ITEK Vault* (Version 1.0.1). Zenodo.https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18436869.

If model outputs are used directly, users are encouraged to:

- Review all cited source documents
- Attribute both ITEK Vault and the original source materials
- Clearly distinguish synthesized model output from original Indigenous Knowledge sources

---

## Intended Use and Limitations

ITEK Vault is designed to assist with literature review, synthesis, and exploratory analysis. It does not replace engagement with Indigenous communities, Knowledge holders, or original source materials.

Model outputs should be treated as interpretive summaries derived from the curated corpus and verified against primary sources before use in decision-making, policy development, or applied research contexts.
